description: Figure 6(a) illustrates the impact of the hyperparameter N on the F1 Score (%) across five different methods: SMD (orange line with square markers), PSM (blue line with circle markers), SWaT (green line with triangle markers), SMAP (purple line with diamond markers), and MSI (yellow line with pentagon markers). The x-axis represents the hyperparameter N, ranging from 0 to 20 with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis shows the F1 Score in percentage, ranging from 70% to 100% with tick marks at 5% intervals. The PSM method consistently achieves the highest F1 Score, starting near 92% at N=0, peaking around 97% at N=5, and gradually declining to approximately 92% at N=20. The SMD method begins at about 87%, rises to a peak of 92% at N=10, then declines to 88% at N=20. The SWaT method starts at 85%, peaks at 91% at N=10, and ends at 88%. The MSI method begins at 85%, dips to 75% at N=5, rises to 87% at N=10, and then declines to 82% at N=20. The SMAP method starts at 73%, rises sharply to 92% at N=10, and then drops to 77% at N=20. Figure 6(b), which is described in the caption as showing the impact of N on AUC, is not visually present in the provided image — only a gray placeholder is shown in its position.
